oneLiner: The world's largest construction and mining equipment maker, now also the AI buildout's power supplier through gensets and turbines. After a sharp de-rating the market is no longer paying for a power annuity at any cost; it is betting on whether 2027 brings margins off the bottom of the target range while the record backlog converts.

verdict.stance: Neutral - backlog delivered, margins still to prove
verdict.summary: Q3 2026 passed our backlog test: orders ran well ahead of shipments in all three segments and power order books now reach 2029-2030. The stock fell anyway, on a moderate Q4 guide and management conceding margins are at the bottom of its target range, and the reset brings the probability-weighted value roughly in line with the live price. The skew is now balanced rather than negative, which is why we move from Cautious to Neutral, not to Positive. The reverse DCF still asks for far more growth than the track record, so the multiple needs margin expansion, not just volume. The January 2027 outlook decides it: a 2027 margin framework off the bottom of the range moves us to Positive; flat margins or a pushout in power shipments sends us back to Cautious.
wtb: Backlog holds at or above $75B at Q4 2026 (late Jan / early Feb 2027) despite the guided Q4 Construction destock, and stays above $70B through 2027.
FY2027 sales grow at least ~8% on a ~$79B FY2026 base (about $85B), with power generation carrying a flat-to-down construction year.
Net margin reaches ~16% in FY2027 (FY2027 EPS ~$30) as volume lifts the adjusted operating margin off the bottom of the target range, excluding any tariff refunds.
The market pays ~21x FY2027 earnings at end-2027, which requires 2028 power orders to look flat-to-up rather than digesting.

bear.why: Hyperscaler 2027 budgets disappoint and data-center customers push out genset and turbine deliveries; backlog shrinks as it converts, construction stays soft after the Q4 2026 destock and capacity depreciation plus tariffs hold margins at the floor. Sales stall near the FY2026 level at a ~13.5% net margin, and the market pays a cyclical multiple on what now looks like peak earnings.

base.why: The backlog converts on schedule and the large-engine and turbine capacity adds ship through 2027; sales grow ~8% to ~$85B (below the ~$88B Street view) as power generation offsets flat construction. Net margin ~16%, roughly the Q3 2026 run-rate, and buybacks cut the count to ~450M. Power visibility earns a premium to the old mid-teens multiple, but not a growth multiple while margins sit at the bottom of the range.

bull.why: Grid scarcity persists: turbine and large-engine slots sell out into 2030, mining re-equips on copper and dealers restock for strong 2027 sales to users. Sales grow ~15% to ~$91B, margins climb toward the middle of the target range (17.5% net) and the market prices Power & Energy as a structural growth franchise.

scenarioModel.note: FY2026 base: Q1-Q3 actual $58.6B ($17.42B + $20.54B + $20.68B) + Q4 ~$20.3B (moderate growth on Q4 2025's $19.13B) = ~$78.9B, +17% on 2025's $67.6B. EPS = revenue x net margin / ~450M diluted shares (460.9M in Q3 2026, falling ~2% a year on buybacks): bear $78B x 13.5% = $10.53B -> $23.4; base $85B x 16.0% = $13.60B -> $30.2; bull $91B x 17.5% = $15.93B -> $35.4. Multiples apply to FY2027 EPS at end-2027: $398 / $635 / $885 per share, probability-weighted ~$638. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Is the power backlog a multi-year annuity or the top of an order cycle?
debates.bull: Orders keep running ahead of shipments: backlog has grown four straight quarters in all three segments, large gas engine orders reach 2029 and turbines 2030, and management says growth is paced by capacity with no 'cliff event'. Alphabet and Amazon both guided 2027 capex meaningfully higher on their Q3 calls.
debates.bear: The backlog roughly doubled in a year on one theme, the 12-month conversion share is drifting down (58% from 59%), CAT still does not disclose the data-center share, and Microsoft trimmed its 2026 capex on third-party data-center delays - the exact pushout mechanism that unwinds industrial backlogs.
debates.view: Our Q3 test (backlog at or above $75B with P&E orders up) was met, which is the main reason we are no longer Cautious. The open risk is timing, not cancellation: a lower conversion share means more of the value sits in 2028-2030.

signpost.metric: Total backlog and Power & Energy order commentary
signpost.threshold: bullish if backlog at or above $78B after the Q4 destock; bearish if below $72B (book-to-bill under 1 for a second quarter)

debates.q: Do margins move off the bottom of the target range in 2027?
debates.bull: Price realization and volume are still outrunning costs, Q4 tariff costs fall ~$200M YoY, Power & Energy margins expanded 250bp in Q3, and management expects margins to start moving off the bottom as volume grows.
debates.bear: Excluding IEEPA refunds the CEO describes margins as 'skipping along the bottom' of the range; freight and depreciation on new capacity rise into Q4, about $2.2B of non-refundable tariffs remain, and Resource Industries margins did not expand in Q3.
debates.view: This is now the debate that sets the multiple (17x vs 25x). The base case needs ~16% net margin; each point of net margin is ~$1.9 of FY2027 EPS. We will judge the January framework ex refunds, not reported.

signpost.metric: 2027 adjusted operating margin outlook excluding tariff refunds
signpost.threshold: above the bottom of the target range for that sales level = bullish (move to Positive); at the bottom or lower = bearish
signpost.when: Q4 2026 report and 2027 outlook, late Jan / early Feb 2027

debates.q: Does the price still ask more than a cyclical can deliver?
debates.bull: Cash conversion is strong (TTM operating cash flow 125% of net income), the diluted count is falling ~1.9% a year, and power is a higher-growth, services-heavy mix, so per-share FCF can outgrow revenue.
debates.bear: Even after the de-rating, the reverse DCF needs ~16.7% a year growth for a decade against ~4.4% a year of revenue growth over the last three fiscal years, and every prior CAT up-cycle ended with earnings and multiple falling together. Net debt of ~$38B (Jun 2026) mostly funds Financial Products, but limits flexibility in a downturn.
debates.view: The bar is still above the track record, so we stay Neutral rather than Positive even with a balanced scenario skew. The 2027 sales guide is the test: below mid-single-digit growth confirms the bar is too high.

signpost.metric: Initial FY2027 sales and revenue growth outlook
signpost.threshold: high-single-digit or better = bar is reachable; flat or down = bear case
signpost.when: Q4 2026 report, late Jan / early Feb 2027

thesis: Power turned the steadiest segment into the growth engine. Power generation sales to users rose 75% in Q3 2026 on data-center turbines and large engines, and orders now reach 2029-2030; capacity, not demand, is the pacing factor.
The order book is still building, not just converting. Backlog rose another ~$6B in Q3 even at record shipments, with growth in all three primary segments for four straight quarters.

Capacity is the moat in power. Large reciprocating engine capacity is planned at nearly 3x the 2024 level by 2030, with a second 3600-series site and the 10MW MaK restart shipping from Q4 2026; rivals face the same lead times and the dealer network turns the installed base into services.
Capital returns compound per share. ME&T free cash flow is guided to the top half of the $6-15B range, funding $7.7B of buybacks in the first nine months of 2026.

latestProse: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30; reported Oct 29). Revenue grew 17% to $20.68B, a hair below consensus, while adjusted EPS of $7.20 beat by about $0.14. All three segments grew double digits; Power & Energy sales to users rose 36% and its margin expanded 250bp, while Resource Industries margins were flat on higher material and tariff costs. Backlog added another ~$6B to a record $78B, but the 12-month conversion share slipped a point. The 10-Q shows $49.4B of obligations on contracts longer than a year, only about a third due within 12 months. On the call the CEO said margins, excluding refunds, are 'skipping along the bottom' of the investor-day target range, with freight and new-capacity depreciation rising. Shares fell ~13% over Oct 29-30, the largest one-day drop in a year, and several brokers cut targets (Morgan Stanley, RBC, Citi, Truist). Enterprise operating cash flow was $4.4B, and $1.9B went to buybacks and dividends.
guidanceProse: FY2026 sales and revenue growth held at the mid-to-high teens (about $79B). Q4 2026 is guided to moderate growth against a tough comparison: Resource Industries strong, Power & Energy moderate, Construction flat with a ~$1.6B seasonal dealer inventory drawdown (vs $0.6B in Q4 2025), though dealer inventory still ends the year ~$0.7B higher. Q4 adjusted operating margin is guided above the prior year, with no further IEEPA recoveries assumed. Full-year tariff cost excluding recoveries is ~$2.2B; recoveries were $520M year to date after the Supreme Court's Feb 2026 IEEPA ruling, with ~$1.2B of recovery receivables outstanding. ME&T free cash flow stays in the top half of the $6-15B range on capex of ~$3.3B (cut from ~$3.5B). The 2027 outlook comes in January; management expects strong 2027 sales to users and margins to start moving off the bottom of the range. Street 2027 revenue sits near $88.4B (TIKR, 17 analysts, Oct 31, 2026).

guide.sub: Held Oct 29 | Q4 moderate growth | 2027 view in Jan

segments: Power & Energy (~41% of Q3 2026 segment sales): reciprocating gensets, Solar Turbines, oil and gas, rail; the data-center growth engine and the highest-margin segment, paced by engine and turbine capacity.
Construction Industries (~37%): North American infrastructure and dealer rental fleets; most exposed to dealer inventory swings, with Q4 volume guided down modestly on the destock.
Resource Industries (~22%): mining trucks and loaders, copper-led re-equipment and autonomy (autonomous trucks targeted at 3x 2024 by 2030); the lowest-margin segment.
Financial Products: dealer and customer financing, roughly $1B of quarterly revenue (unverified exact); carries most of the consolidated debt.
competitive: Cummins (CMI): the closest fight in data-center gensets; both are capacity-constrained on large engines.
Rolls-Royce (mtu), Wartsila, Generac and GE Vernova (large gas turbines): chase the same power backlog; none pairs it with CAT's dealer-and-services footprint across construction and mining.
Komatsu: the global number two in construction and mining equipment; competes on price and currency.
Deere (DE): ag-heavy mix; it rose on CAT's Q3 day, a sign the selloff was CAT-specific rather than sector-wide.
moat: The dealer network is the moat: the largest independent dealer organization locks in parts, service and financing over a machine population measured in decades, turning services into an annuity on installed iron. In power, large-engine and turbine manufacturing scale plus a multi-year order book form a capacity moat rivals cannot quickly replicate.
risks: Order-cycle reversal. The backlog nearly doubled YoY on one theme and CAT does not disclose the data-center share; Microsoft already cut its 2026 capex on third-party data-center delays, and pushouts would lower the conversion share further.

Valuation bar above the track record. The reverse DCF still needs ~16.7% a year growth for a decade against ~4.4% a year revenue growth over three fiscal years; in the bear case EPS and the multiple compress together, a loss of over a third.

Margins stuck at the floor. Excluding refunds the adjusted margin sits at the bottom of the target range, ~$2.2B of tariffs remain and capacity depreciation rises; refund timing depends on CBP and is not in the Q4 guide.
Capacity added into a possible peak. A multi-year plan to nearly triple large-engine capacity creates absorption risk if 2028-2029 orders slow.
Construction and macro. The ~$1.6B Q4 dealer destock tests retail demand; China construction stays weak and higher rates gate non-residential activity.
catalysts: Q4 2026: first 10MW MaK engine shipments and ~$1.6B Construction dealer destock (debates 1, 2).
Late Jan / early Feb 2027 (date unverified): MSFT, GOOGL, META, AMZN Q4 calls with 2027 capex budgets, Meta's first (debate 1).
Late Jan / early Feb 2027 (date unverified): Q4 2026 results, backlog and the first 2027 outlook including the margin framework (debates 1, 2, 3).
Ongoing: CBP review of IEEPA refund claims (~$1.2B receivable) - upside to reported margins, excluded from our margin test (debate 2).
Late Apr 2027 (unverified): Q1 2027 results - first quarter of capacity-add shipments at scale (debate 1).

valPresets.note: Base-year FCF is cyclically elevated (record margins, backlog conversion), so presets are deliberately modest and fade to a 2.5% terminal. Bear models a post-boom FCF decline, base a GDP-plus glide, bull a sustained power-scarcity ramp. Even the bull preset sits well below the ~16.7% a year the reverse DCF says is priced in.
